links.outcome: Whether AI-assisted decisions differed by patient race and gender in randomized vignettes
links.effect: Physician decision accuracy improved significantly with GPT-4 advice without introducing or exacerbating existing race or gender biases (abstract-level result; no numbers given in the text).
links.quote: Results showed that physicians are willing to change their initial clinical impressions given AI assistance, and that this led to a significant improvement in clinical decision-making accuracy in a chest pain evaluation scenario without introducing or exacerbating existing race or gender biases.

links.outcome: Physician decision accuracy before versus after receiving ChatGPT+ advice on chest pain vignettes
links.effect: Pre-post comparison showed a significant improvement in clinical decision-making accuracy after AI assistance (no numeric estimates in the text).

screen.reason: The study empirically tests the effect of providing ChatGPT advice to physicians (clinician decision-making with vs. without AI assistance) on diagnostic accuracy and demographic bias in a randomized clinical vignette study.
